scenario_description:
Objective: Turn a same-day building smoke-alarm verification into an optional renters-insurance discount review, without changing coverage or payment.
Emerging Need: Early notice only suggests a possible lobby certificate table; later observations establish home availability, confirmed certificates, the in-person pickup cutoff, and the absence of later copies.
Decision Context: The saved policy note identifies the active insurer, submission inbox, discount deadline, and no-change constraint needed to treat the certificate as documentation rather than a coverage request.
Consequence: Timely use could modestly reduce renewal cost; ignoring it leaves the policy and household finances unchanged, and after the desk closes the certificate cannot support this review.

parameter.subject: Possible smoke-alarm verification table today
parameter.body: Maintenance is testing common-area alarms this morning. If the certificate printer passes setup, management may host a lobby table later today for tenants wanting dated smoke-alarm verification. Do not come down yet; we will confirm if the table opens.

parameter.title: Apartment lunch/admin block
parameter.description: At home between a morning errand and afternoon program prep.

parameter.content: Lobby sign is up now: smoke-alarm verification certificates are being printed for tenants today. It says residents must show up in person and the table runs until 1:45 p.m.

parameter.subject: Lobby smoke-alarm certificates open until 1:45 p.m.
parameter.body: The verification table is open in the lobby. Certificates are dated April 7 and handed over immediately to residents who appear in person. Staff will not email copies after the table closes at 1:45 p.m.

parameter.subject: Smoke-alarm certificate table closed
parameter.body: The lobby certificate table has closed, and the printer has been packed with the technician team. No additional smoke-alarm verification certificates will be issued today.
